Among banks that anticipated stronger demand, the most cited reason for this outlook, chosen by

In a last special question, banks were asked about which credit scoring models were important to 
them when approving credit card applications. While the most selected option was credit bureau 
scores, chosen by almost all respondents, a major share of banks also selected internal behavioral 
scores as an important factor for their approval decisions. A significant share of banks also 
indicated that third-party behavioral credit scores were important.
